text:
alex.kaplan: ran a sticky KV-prefetching sweep on ggml-int8-llama2-large with extended ctx (64k). trying to reproduce the divergence we saw in yesterday's rollout. results are weird :thinking:

maya.r: quick summary?

alex.kaplan: short: avg latency +4ms p50, p99 +22ms, but token-level divergence after ~12k tokens in some traces. cache hit rate looked high overall (89%) yet we see repeated evictions around window boundaries.

 tom_s: did you change the prefetch stride?

alex.kaplan: yes — enabled sticky-prefetch with stride=4096 (keeps the prefetched pages pinned to the same slot until the window shifts). hypothesis: when the requested context slides across a backend shard boundary, the sticky pages get remapped and we accidentally duplicate KV segments -> divergence.

 eva_ml: can you paste the repro command and a short log?

alex.kaplan: sure:
```bash
# repro command used on staging-ia-4
./run_inference --model ggml-int8-llama2-large \n  --ctx 65536 --prefetch sticky --prefetch-stride 4096 \n  --batch 1 --seqs 1 --seed 42 --trace-kv
```

log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18 14:22:11.901] kv: prefetch page 0x7ffb8 size=4096 -> slot 12
[2026-03-18 14:22:11.902] kv: prefetch page 0x803c4 size=4096 -> slot 12 (sticky)
[2026-03-18 14:22:12.011] kv: window shift +4096 -> remap slots
[2026-03-18 14:22:12.012] kv: detect duplicate segment id=0x1f4 -> evict slot 12
[2026-03-18 14:22:12.013] kv: cache-miss index=81920
[2026-03-18 14:22:12.014] kv: token divergence detected at token_idx=12345 -> model_output checksum mismatch
```

maya.r: do we only see this with sticky mode? what about LRU prefetch?

alex.kaplan: tried LRU-prefetch w/ same stride: no divergence, slightly higher latency (+6ms p50) but stable outputs. suggests the issue is the pinning semantics.

tom_s: interesting — maybe our remap logic assumes idempotent page placement. if sticky keeps old slot indices and a remap occurs, we can end up with two pages for same logical index.

eva_ml: can you attach the eval diff (perplexity + token-accuracy) vs baseline?

alex.kaplan: attaching quick numbers inline:
- baseline (no prefetch): ppl=14.8, token-acc@1000=0.9923
- LRU-prefetch: ppl=14.9, token-acc@1000=0.9919
- sticky-prefetch (broken traces): ppl=15.3, token-acc@1000=0.9864

maya.r: that's a meaningful regression in downstream metrics. do we have a minimal repro that isolates remap?

alex.kaplan: yes. small harness that alternates requests so the client-visible context straddles the boundary every ~4k tokens. pushing a gist to staging artifacts. link: https://artifacts.redwood/test-run/1987654321/repro.tar.gz

ci-bot: created issue #421: "kv sticky-prefetch remap -> duplicate segments" and attached logs. (CI run id: 20260318-881)
tom_s: thanks. proposed quick fix: when remap occurs, validate physical slot content vs logical segment id and evict only if ids mismatch, otherwise move metadata instead of naive evict. cheaper short-term patch.

eva_ml: can we also add a unit test to the remapper to force sticky allocations and ensure idempotency?

alex.kaplan: yep. i'll implement patch + unit test, run the quant-int8 perf sweep and post numbers. planning to revert sticky-prefetch on prod until we confirm. :+1:

maya.r: thanks — also flagging for canary config so Dedicated customers don't hit this in rollout.

alex.kaplan: updated the ticket with rollout guard and a smoke script. leaving notes for QA: run with --ctx 65536 and the alternating-window harness.

tom_s: great. if you want I can help with the kernel-level validation tomorrow morning.

alex.kaplan: thanks, appreciate it. :eyes:
